deities: Harihar (united Shiva-Vishnu form - the dham's namesake)

history.period: Construction began ~1990; about 30 years to complete the Shivlinga; temple trust formed 1996
history.summary: Harihar Dham at Bagodar is a modern Shiva temple famed for its 65-ft (20 m) Shivlinga, widely reported as one of the tallest in the world; one source says it is carved from a single dark stone standing uncovered under the open sky. The complex spans ~25 acres, is surrounded by a river, and includes smaller shrines for Parvati, Ganesha, Hanuman and Vishnu; a small Shivling inside the main linga is the one actually worshipped. The deity is venerated as Harihar, uniting Shiva and Vishnu. (CSV town 'Giridih' is the district headquarters; the temple is actually at Bagodar, ~60 km south-west of Giridih town on NH-100.)

name: Harihar Dham
town_description: Bagodar is a block headquarters town in Giridih district on the Grand Trunk Road (NH-19), about 60 km south-west of Giridih town; Harihar Dham lies ~3 km off the highway. (CSV town 'Giridih' is the district headquarters; corrected to Bagodar.)
tradition: Hinduism (Shaivism, with Vaishnava element in the Harihar form)

travel.airport: Ranchi (Birsa Munda Airport) is the nearest major airport (~150-160 km).
travel.railway: Hazaribagh Road station is ~10 km away; Chichaki is ~18.6 km; Giridih Junction connects onward.
travel.road: ~3 km from the Grand Trunk Road at Bagodar on NH-100, about 60 km south-west of Giridih district headquarters.

visitor_information.best_time: September to February (winter); Shravan month draws the largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily (corroborated by two listings).
